svg.title: Interactive Journey UI Design — Report & Q&A (US SBS Credit & Risk, case 366132845011)
svg.text: 1. Why and how the default occurred?
for bankruptcy — reactive attempts to access credit.
– Feb 2025: Global limit reduced and letter requested —
– Jan 2025: Outbound calls with no contact or message only
– Sep 2025: Balance accelerated, referred O/A CPE 1.0 with
O/A code 42 — formal recognition of default.
– Sep 2025: Proactive cancellation processed and delivered
External revolving utilization held at 92–93%, Jan–Apr 2024.
Amex ≥ 40% of overall exposure through Jan–Dec 2024.
Both model scores stayed below threshold Aug–Dec 2024 —
Risk drivers: inquiry activity, elevated balance and utilization,
high pay-in-full amounts, merchant spend concentration.
Bottom drivers: stable bureau score, limited delinquency
Largely below threshold Feb–Jun 2025, with one structural-risk
Drivers shift to weak paydown, rising asset stress and internal
Any spending spikes? What are the drivers for it?
In this case, how did TSR and CDSS react? While the TSR and CDSS
were reacting, how was the bureau profile?
Fig 1 · TSR and CDSS vs their own risky thresholds; bureau profile read over the same window (Fig 2).
Summarize the abnormal transactions when TSR was
Reaction window read as 2025-03 → 2025-06 (TSR above 20, peak 27.4 in Apr 2025):
12 charges at AMAZON MARKEPLACE NA PA in that window — 4× this account’s typical merchant frequency.
Three same-day pairs at one merchant, each above the 90th-percentile ticket for the account.

Ask a follow-up about this case…
Screen passed · in scope · outcome completed

svg.text: Spend spiked in May 2025 and TSR reacted the following month;
the abnormal merchant cluster falls inside that window, so the
behaviour and the score reaction are the same episode.
Orchestrator consulted the Report agent and constructed a team of
2 domain specialists, dispatched in parallel on this turn:
sub-question: Which transactions are abnormal while TSR was
reacting? Report merchant, amount and date at row level, and state the
yardstick used to call them abnormal.
sub-question: Over which months was TSR reacting? Bound the
window using each metric’s own risky threshold, and date the peak.
sub-question: Do the curated reports describe abnormal spend in
this window? Cite explicit rows; if not mentioned, state so clearly.
12 charges at AMAZON MARKEPLACE NA PA between 2025-03 and
2025-06 — 4× this account’s typical merchant frequency. Three
same-day pairs sit above the 90th-percentile ticket.
Median ticket 2,140 vs 8,760 for the three flagged pairs.
2 of 12 charges fall outside the window and are excluded.
TSR sat above its threshold (20) from 2025-03 to 2025-06, peaking
at 27.4 in Apr 2025; CDSS never crossed its own threshold of 10.
Window handed to the spends specialist to bound its scan.
Both specialists were dispatched from one team_plan and completed
independently; synthesis waits for the slower of the two (5.12 s).
The curated reports describe elevated merchant spend
concentration in this period but do not enumerate individual
transactions. The April 2025 structural-risk breach is stated
“…fluctuating below 20 except for a breach in April (27.4)…”
12 charges at a single merchant cluster inside the TSR
The window comes from the modeling specialist, not from
Abnormality is measured against a stated yardstick — 4×
Reports corroborate the concentration but not the rows.
